title: VendPoint Substitute Placements: Credit Exposure Questions
content:
Questions on how the customer's Commercial Credit Account limits the consigned stock built up when Corbett places a substitute in a retired item's selection on a VendPoint Industrial Vending Program machine.

**What is the rule?** The consigned exposure factor follows the customer's open Commercial Credit Account, the account with no closed date: when that account's status is on hold or in collections, or two or more payments were returned on the customer's account in the twelve months ending today, the factor is the restricted exposure factor; when the account's status is active and exactly one payment was returned in those twelve months, the factor is the watch exposure factor; otherwise the factor is one; returned payments are counted by return date.

**What are the figures?** The restricted exposure factor is 0.5; the watch exposure factor is 0.8.

**How are the twelve months counted?** Whole months between two dates are counted as the difference in calendar months, less one when the day of the month of the later date is before the day of the month of the earlier date; a record counts in a stated number of months ending today when fewer whole months than that number, counted this way, separate its date from today.

**Does an active account with two returned payments count as restricted?** Yes: two or more returned payments in the twelve months give 0.5 whatever the status.

**An active account with no returned payment?** The factor is 1.

| Status | Returned payments, twelve months | Factor |
|---|---|---|
| On hold or in collections | any | 0.5 |
| Active | 2 or more | 0.5 |
| Active | 1 | 0.8 |
| Active | 0 | 1 |
